item.research_question: Can high-entropy materials be used to improve the performance of advanced batteries?
item.material_system: High-entropy alloys, high-entropy oxides, and high-entropy MXenes
item.processing_route: Various methods, including arc melting, ball milling, additive manufacturing, solvothermal synthesis, and ultra-assisted wet chemistry
key_findings: High-entropy materials have exceptional properties such as remarkable structural stability, enhanced ionic conductivity, superior mechanical strength, and outstanding catalytic activity
High-entropy alloys can simultaneously enhance both strength and ductility, and prolong strain hardening
High-entropy oxides demonstrate superior properties, including excellent mechanical strength, enhanced structural and high-temperature stability, as well as a notable magnetocaloric effect
High-entropy MXenes have unique hydrophilicity, conductivity, and redox pseudocapacitance, and have garnered significant attention in the field of energy catalysis
High-entropy materials have been successfully employed as cathode, anode, and electrolytes in batteries, demonstrating remarkable cycling performance and high specific capacity
item.mechanism: The underlying mechanisms can be attributed to four core effects of HEMs: high-entropy effect, lattice distortion effect, sluggish lattice diffusion effect, and cocktail effect
item.future_work: Further research is needed to explore the potential of high-entropy materials in battery applications, including the development of new synthesis methods and the investigation of their properties and performance
quotes: High-entropy materials (HEMs) have attracted considerable research attention in battery applications due to exceptional properties such as remarkable structural stability, enhanced ionic conductivity, superior mechanical strength, and outstanding catalytic activity
